artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $n \geq 3$, let $D_{\text{no3}\ell}(n)$ denote the minimum, over all sets $P$ of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that no three points of $P$ are collinear, of the number of distinct values in the multiset $\{\,\|p-q\|_2 : p,q \in P,\ p \neq q\,\}$, where $\|\cdot\|_2$ denotes the Euclidean distance. It is known that
$$\left\lceil \tfrac{n-1}{3} \right\rceil \le D_{\text{no3}\ell}(n) \le \left\lfloor \tfrac{n}{2} \right\rfloor,$$
the upper bound being attained by suitable configurations and the lower bound being due to Szemerédi. Szemerédi conjectured that $D_{\text{no3}\ell}(n) = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

Determine the exact value of $D_{\text{no3}\ell}(n)$ as a function of $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact value of the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set in general position (no three collinear) is not known. Szemerédi's lower bound ⌈(n−1)/3⌉ has been slightly improved (e.g., Dumitrescu's 13n/36 − O(1) and subsequent small improvements via bounds on isosceles triangles), but neither matches the conjectured value ⌊n/2⌋. The conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.claim: The exact value is posed as an open problem with conjectured value ⌊n/2⌋.

status_evidence.title: Points in General Position — Some Plane Truths
status_evidence.snippet: Lower bound improvements over Szemerédi's ⌈(n−1)/3⌉ via bounds on isosceles triangles, with Dumitrescu's 13n/36 − O(1) and further small improvements.
status_evidence.claim: Best known lower bounds are still well below ⌊n/2⌋, indicating the problem is unresolved.
